segments.title: How Britain might react to an F-14 decades early
segments.summary: Britain in the 1940s or 1950s would probably welcome an F-14A Tomcat and try to figure out how it worked.
segments.body: The question imagines Britain receiving an F-14A Tomcat in the 1940s or 1950s and asks whether studying its design would leave the British unhappy with a flaw. In this alternate-history scenario, the expected reaction is enthusiasm and an attempt to understand technology from a later era. The brief answer does not assess the suggested flaw or discuss particular systems and the limits on reproducing them.
segments.question: If Britain received an F-14A Tomcat in the 1940s or 1950s, would studying it leave the British unhappy with a design flaw?
segments.answerShort: They would probably be very happy to receive it and would try to figure out how it worked.

evidence.note: A viewer asks whether the British would study an F-14A received in the 1940s or 1950s and be unhappy with a design flaw. Dr. Clarke thinks they would be very happy with it and would try to figure it out. No specific flaw is assessed before the discussion returns to the OBS test.
